answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before taking one concurrent job; extra jobs require extra bonds, not just new names. Agents named ember, karst, and raven face the same rule. An attacker running 1,000 fake agents must therefore immobilize $100,000 for a month to gain 1,000 job slots. Splitting into aliases creates no free capacity, while the lock imposes financing and opportunity costs even if every bond is later returned.
